//: Drawing notation -> catalog FAMILY + the variant axes that make it a real stock item. catalog.json entries are families ('Set A - max 160A', '3P/4P'), not orderable products, so a family id alone is never a valid stock key. Read by both the Gemini prompt and the server matcher. Seeded from 3918.24-12-1 — verify the variant letters against what you actually stock.
//series: series -> which catalog family it belongs to, and which axes must be known before it can be stocked. Missing any listed axis = incomplete, send to review, do not create a stock line.
//axes: Legal values per axis. class is the ABB breaking-capacity letter — CONFIRM THIS LIST, it is the whole reason a stock line is distinct. Drawing said XT1D.
//notation: What the drawing writes -> series plus any variant it encodes in the model number itself.
//stockKey: How a resolved component becomes a partID. Axes in the order listed under series, uppercased, joined with |. Example: abb-tmax-xt1|D|3P|100A. Family id alone is never a stock key.
//uncatalogued: Seen on real drawings, deliberately absent from catalog.json. Listed so the model treats these as expected misses rather than failures — stops it substituting a similar ABB part.
